content.value_statement: Code changes often become harder to read after fast iteration. This skill reviews recent edits and refines structure, naming, and consistency without changing behavior.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recently modified code for readability and maintainability issues.
Applies project coding standards from the active repository context.
Simplifies unnecessary nesting, redundant logic, and unclear naming.
Preserves existing behavior while improving code structure.
Keeps useful abstractions when they improve organization or debugging.
Documents only significant changes that affect understanding.
limitations: It depends on available project context and recent edits.
It does not prove behavior is unchanged without tests.
It may need user direction for broad or architectural refactors.
It is designed for code refinement, not feature design.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Feature Work
use_cases.description: Refine code after building a feature so it is easier to review, test, and maintain.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Improve consistency and readability before opening a pull request for team review.

use_cases.title: Improve React Components
use_cases.description: Simplify component logic, props, naming, and conditional rendering while preserving the user experience.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Recent Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simplify skill to review my recent code changes. Improve readability and consistency without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Local Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Simplify the files I changed in this session. Follow the repository conventions and explain any important cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Component Complexity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the modified React components. Reduce unnecessary nesting, improve names, and keep behavior identical.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Before Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my current diff for maintainability. Simplify only touched code, preserve public behavior, and leave helpful abstractions intact.

output_examples.input: A recently edited component has nested conditionals, unclear variable names, and repeated rendering logic.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a clearer component structure, better names, and a short note about the behavior-preserving cleanup.

output_examples.input: A utility function works correctly but has redundant branches and comments that repeat the code.
output_examples.output: The skill removes redundancy, keeps meaningful names, and reports the simplification without adding unrelated changes.

output_examples.input: A pull request has several touched files that mix styles and inconsistent error handling.
output_examples.output: The skill aligns the edited code with project style and identifies any cleanup that needs test verification.

best_practices: Run tests after simplification to confirm behavior stayed the same.
Use the skill after completing a focused code change.
Keep the review scope limited to files touched in the current session.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to rewrite stable code without a clear scope.
Do not accept cleanup that changes behavior without review.
Do not replace helpful abstractions only to reduce line count.

faq.question: What does this skill improve?
faq.answer: It improves readability, naming, structure, and project consistency in recently modified code.

faq.question: Does it change how the code behaves?
faq.answer: It is designed to preserve behavior, but tests should confirm important workflows.

faq.question: Can it review an entire repository?
faq.answer: It focuses on recent changes unless you explicitly ask for a broader review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for TypeScript or React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for explicit types, React props, and component clarity.

faq.question: Should I run tests after using it?
faq.answer: Yes. Tests are the best way to verify that simplification preserved behavior.
